title: Judge Kelly Issues 14-Day Restraining Order Restoring CNN, MS NOW and Politico's White House Access
detail: US District Judge Timothy Kelly ruled Thursday, September 24, 2026, that CNN, MS NOW and Politico had 'shown a likelihood of success' on their Fifth Amendment due-process claims and ordered the Trump administration to immediately restore the outlets' White House press credentials for 14 days. Kelly found the outlets' hard passes were 'revoked without constitutionally adequate due process,' and rejected the administration's national-security justification, noting Trump's own stated reason for the ban focused on 'the alleged lack of truthfulness and negativity' of the coverage. Despite the order, journalists from all three outlets were turned away again Thursday morning and had passes confiscated by Secret Service before the White House began reinstating credentials around 7:25 a.m. ET. The ruling isn't immediately appealable; Kelly set a schedule for further briefing over the next two weeks.

media.caption: A federal judge ordered the White House to restore CNN, MS NOW and Politico's press access for 14 days, finding their credentials were revoked without due process

title: White House Blocks CNN and MS NOW From Covering Xi State Dinner Arrivals Hours After Court-Ordered Reinstatement
detail: Hours after Judge Kelly's restraining order restored their credentials, CNN and MS NOW editorial staff were again denied entry Thursday evening, September 24, 2026, when they tried to cover arrivals for President Trump's state dinner honoring Xi Jinping. CNN senior White House correspondent Kristen Holmes said officials told the network only camera and audio staff — not editorial personnel — would be admitted to the pre-credentialed press event, while Politico's reporter was also turned away. CNN anchor Erin Burnett said 'CNN did not refuse to cover the event. We, like MS NOW and Politico, were denied access to the White House grounds,' and CNN's Jake Tapper called it 'another egregious violation of the First Amendment and the judge's order.' Trump alleged the networks had refused to cover Xi's arrival to avoid giving him credit for the visit.

media.caption: CNN correspondent Betsy Klein reports from outside the White House after CNN and MS NOW editorial staff were again denied entry, this time to cover Xi Jinping's state dinner arrivals

title: US and China Extend Trade Truce Through January 10 as Xi Attends White House State Arrival Ceremony
detail: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Thursday, September 24, 2026, that the US and China had extended their trade truce — first reached in Busan in October 2025 — by two months, through January 10, 2027, rather than letting it lapse on November 10 as previously scheduled; China's rare-earth export-control threat was also delayed to the same date. Current US tariffs on Chinese goods stand at roughly 36.5%, with Chinese tariffs on US goods around 31%. The announcement coincided with Xi's formal White House arrival: a State Arrival Ceremony on the South Lawn featured roughly 479 US service members, a Marine Corps Silent Drill Platoon salute, and a flyover of a B-2 Spirit bomber with four F-22 Raptors, before Trump told Xi 'the ties between our people endure, and we've never gotten along better' and Xi described a US-China friendship 'forged in blood and fire' dating to World War II. The day closed with a state dinner in the East Room attended by tech executives including Elon Musk, Tim Cook, Sam Altman and Jensen Huang. Analysts cautioned the truce extension addresses immediate friction — soybean purchases, tariff pauses — without resolving deeper disputes over export controls, Taiwan and China's ties to Iran.

media.caption: Trump and Xi at the White House State Arrival Ceremony, held the same day the US and China extended their trade truce through January 10, 2027
